conductingBody: Staff Selection Commission (SSC), Government of India
overview: SSC CGL is a national exam held by the Staff Selection Commission. It fills Group B and Group C posts in central government ministries, departments and offices. Examples are Assistant Section Officer, Inspector (Income Tax, Central Excise, Posts), Auditor, Accountant, Tax Assistant and Junior Statistical Officer. CGL 2026 has two computer-based tiers. Tier-I is only a screening test. The final merit list uses Tier-II marks only. Any graduate can apply, but a few posts need a specific degree or subject. The SSC notice of 24 September 2026 gives 10,731 tentative vacancies. Tier-I runs from 30 September to 30 October 2026.

pattern.mode: Computer Based Examination (online, objective multiple-choice questions)
pattern.duration: 1 hour. Each of the 4 sections has its own 15-minute timer. Candidates eligible for a scribe get 1 hour 20 minutes (20 minutes per section).
pattern.marking: 2 marks for each correct answer (50 marks for 25 questions). 0.50 mark is cut for each wrong answer.
notes: Questions come in English and Hindi, except the English Comprehension section.
Minimum qualifying marks: UR 30%, OBC/EWS 25%, all other categories 20%.
Tier-I is for shortlisting only. Its marks are not added to the final merit list.
SSC fixes separate Tier-I cut-offs for (a) JSO and Statistical Investigator Grade-II, (b) Assistant Audit Officer and Assistant Accounts Officer, and (c) all other posts.
If the exam runs in many shifts, marks are normalized using SSC's published method.
Reasoning, General Awareness and English questions are at graduation level. Quantitative Aptitude questions are at Class 10 level.

pattern.mode: Computer Based Examination (objective MCQs, plus one typing task)
pattern.duration: Session-I: 2 hours 15 minutes (Section-I 1 hour, Section-II 1 hour, Section-III 15 minutes). Session-II: 15 minutes for the Data Entry Speed Test, on the same day. Scribe-eligible candidates get extra time.

sections.name: Section-I B: Reasoning and General Intelligence
Section-II A: English Language and Comprehension
Section-IV: Data Entry Speed Test (qualifying only)

pattern.marking: 3 marks for each correct answer. 1 mark is cut for each wrong answer in Sections I, II and III.
notes: Section-I has a 30-minute timer for each subject. Section-II gives 40 minutes for English and 20 minutes for General Awareness.
You must qualify every section of Paper-I separately.
Only Sections I and II (390 marks) count for merit. Sections III and IV are qualifying only.
Data Entry Speed Test: type a passage of about 2,000 key presses in 15 minutes. Maximum errors allowed: UR 20%, OBC/EWS 25%, others 30%.

Some posts (for example ASO in CSS/MEA/AFHQ, CBIC Inspectors and Executive Assistant, Postal/Sorting Assistant, Tax Assistant) need higher qualifying standards in the computer test and/or typing test.
Mathematics is at Class 10 level and English at Class 12 level.
The final merit list is made from Tier-II marks only.

pattern.duration: 2 hours (2 hours 40 minutes for scribe-eligible candidates)
pattern.marking: 2 marks for each correct answer. 0.50 mark is cut for each wrong answer.
notes: Only candidates who applied for these posts and are shortlisted for them in Tier-I take this paper.
Merit for these posts uses Paper-I Sections I and II plus Paper-II.

pattern.duration: 2 hours (2 hours 40 minutes for scribe-eligible candidates)

eligibility.nationality: You must be a citizen of India, or a subject of Nepal or Bhutan. A person of Indian origin who migrated from Pakistan, Burma, Sri Lanka, Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Zambia, Malawi, Zaire, Ethiopia or Vietnam to settle permanently in India can also apply. Everyone except Indian citizens needs an eligibility certificate from the Government of India before getting a job offer.

age.summary: Age is counted as on 1 August 2026. The limit depends on the post. 18–27 years (born between 2 Aug 1999 and 1 Aug 2008): all Pay Level 4 and 5 Group C posts, such as Auditor, Accountant, Tax Assistant, UDC/SSA and Postal/Sorting Assistant. 20–30 years (born between 2 Aug 1996 and 1 Aug 2006): ASO in CSS, Ministry of Railways, MEA and AFHQ, and Sub Inspector in CBI. 18–30 years (born between 2 Aug 1996 and 1 Aug 2008): most other Group B posts. 18–32 years (born between 2 Aug 1994 and 1 Aug 2008): Junior Statistical Officer.

education.posts: Assistant Audit Officer (State Cadre) and Assistant Accounts Officer (State Cadre)
education.requirement: Bachelor's degree, plus the ability to read, write, speak and understand the state's regional/official language at Class 10 level, with a certificate from a recognised board. Same desirable qualifications as the Central Cadre post.
Bachelor's degree in any subject with at least 60% marks in Mathematics in Class 12, OR a Bachelor's degree in any subject with Statistics as one of the subjects in the degree.

education.posts: Statistical Investigator Grade-II (Ministry of Home Affairs)
education.requirement: Bachelor's degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Economics, Demography, Population Studies, Operations Research, Information Technology, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Computer Technology, Computer Application, Data Science or Artificial Intelligence.
You can apply, but you must have the required degree, with the result declared, on or before 1 August 2026.

other: The education cut-off date is 1 August 2026. A result that the university is still processing on that date does not count.
Degrees through open and distance learning count only if the university was approved by the UGC Distance Education Bureau for that period.
Only male candidates can be selected for vacancies in the Border Roads Organisation (BRO).

Some posts need physical and medical standards. These include CBIC Inspectors, Inspector and Sub-Inspector in CBN, Sub-Inspector/JIO in NCB, Sub-Inspector in CBI and NIA, and UDC/SSA in BRO. The department checks these after final selection.
Ex-servicemen who are only matriculates can apply for Group C ex-servicemen vacancies only, and only if they have at least 15 years of service.
Application fee: ₹100. Women, SC, ST, PwBD and eligible ex-servicemen candidates do not pay any fee.
Selected Assistant Audit Officers and Assistant Accounts Officers must pass a departmental exam during probation to be confirmed.
Posts carry All India Service Liability, so you can be posted anywhere in India.

faqs.q: When is the SSC CGL 2026 Tier-I exam?
faqs.a: SSC's notice of 12 September 2026 says Tier-I runs from 30 September to 30 October 2026. Your admit card is expected 2–3 days before your own exam date. Tier-II is tentatively planned for December 2026.

faqs.q: How many vacancies are there in SSC CGL 2026?
faqs.a: SSC lists 10,731 tentative vacancies as on 24 September 2026. The first notice of 21 May 2026 said about 12,256. Final numbers may still change.

faqs.q: What is the age limit for SSC CGL 2026?
faqs.a: Age is counted as on 1 August 2026. Depending on the post, the limit is 18–27, 20–30, 18–30 or 18–32 years (18–32 is for JSO). SC/ST get 5 more years, OBC 3 years and PwBD 10 years.

Yes. In Tier-I, 0.50 mark is cut for each wrong answer (a correct answer gets 2 marks). In Tier-II Paper-I, 1 mark is cut per wrong answer in Sections I–III (a correct answer gets 3 marks). In Papers II and III, 0.50 mark is cut per wrong answer.

faqs.q: Do Tier-I marks count in the final selection?
faqs.a: No. Tier-I is only used to shortlist candidates for Tier-II. The final merit list uses Tier-II marks only: Sections I and II of Paper-I, plus Paper-II or Paper-III for the posts that need them.

faqs.q: What were the Tier-I cut-offs in CGL 2025?
faqs.a: For all posts except JSO and SI Grade-II, the corrected official cut-offs (out of 200) were: UR 136.40, OBC 130.37, EWS 127.42, SC 115.03 and ST 106.39. Cut-offs change every year.

calculator.note: Tier-I has 100 questions for 200 marks, and 0.50 mark is cut for each wrong answer (CGL 2026 notice, para 13.8). This gives your raw score. SSC normalizes marks across shifts, so your official score may be different.
